title: Civil Defense Siren
description:
2 PM — a siren suddenly goes off.
Civil defense drill. Twice a year, this siren briefly pauses all of Seoul.

One of the first things that shocks foreigners.
For Koreans: 'oh, this again.'

choices.text: Follow the drill — look for the shelter signs
choices.result_text:
Walked toward the subway station. Yellow shelter signs.

You knew it was a drill, but your body moved before your mind did.
The things you rehearse in peacetime are what save you when it counts.

choices.text: It's just a drill — keep drinking my coffee
choices.result_text:
Everyone in the café stayed put. You did too.

The siren stopped and Seoul started moving again. Five minutes.
In this country, a crisis is a one-sip pause in your coffee.

title: A Friend Enlists
description:
A KakaoTalk message from a friend:
"I enlist next month. Might not be able to reach me for 2 years."

For Korean men, military service is not a choice.
18 months to 2 years — it gets written into the timeline toward Gangnam.

choices.text: Promise a discharge gift: 'I'll buy dinner when you're out'
choices.result_text:
'Samgyeopsal's on you when you get out.' you sent it.
'If you're living in Gangnam by then, let's eat there.' He sent back.

That joke warmed you. There's someone who can picture two years from now with you.

'Take care.' Three words.

Should have said more, maybe. But you didn't know what.
You still don't know what to say to a friend heading to the army.

title: Reserve Duty Notice
description:
A text arrives:
'Reserve Forces Training Notice. Date: [Month] [Day] 09:00. No-show fine: ₩1,500,000.'

[Military reserve duty: all Korean men serve 18–21 months of active duty, then remain in the reserve for 8 more years after discharge. Once a year (sometimes more), they're called back for drills. Miss one without an approved reason: ₩1.5M fine. It's not optional, and it lands on your schedule whether you're planning a job interview or a business pitch.]

Another day blocked off. Another reminder that some things in Korea aren't negotiable.

choices.text: Clear the schedule and go dutifully
choices.result_text:
Up early, training grounds. Camo cream on, whole day gone.

Something strangely comfortable about being with fellow reservists. Like slipping out of the world for a day.
Stood there and told myself: back to society tomorrow, back to working hard.

Searched the exemption criteria list. Overseas residence, illness, sole breadwinner...

Not applicable. I have to go either way.
But checking the options is my way. If you don't look, you get blindsided.

title: North Korea in the News
description:
Breaking news alert: 'North Korea fires missile — falls into East Sea.'

Seoul is quiet. The stock market dips for a moment, then recovers.
Foreign friends send KakaoTalk messages: 'Are you okay?'

choices.text: Reply: 'Yeah, I'm fine — this just happens here'
choices.result_text:
'Don't worry, this happens all the time here.' Sent.

True. For Koreans, North Korea news is like weather news.
It exists — but it doesn't change today's plans.

choices.text: Check the market movement — geopolitical risk
choices.result_text:
KOSPI dropped 0.4%, then recovered. Brief foreign sell-off.

Geopolitical risk is a structural discount on Korean stocks, you once read.
Means nothing to your bank account today — but it's knowledge you'll use someday.

title: Korea-US Relations
description:
US election results are in.
Korean media pivots instantly to the Korea-US alliance and defense cost-sharing.
The won-dollar exchange rate starts to move.

choices.text: Watch the exchange rate — USD deposits cross my mind
choices.result_text:
When the dollar rises, Korean won assets weaken in relative terms.
Conversely, if you hold USD deposits, this could be your moment.

No money to act on it, but you understand the structure now.
Understanding comes first. Execution comes later.

choices.text: Focus on my own life — can't change superpower politics
choices.result_text:
Turned off the news.

Korea-US relations, exchange rates — things you can't change.
Decided to focus on what you can change. Got back to today's task.
